senses.gloss: m.(b. h. מֹלֶךְ)Molekh, the fire-god of the Canaanites and others.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 7:7">Snh. VII, 7</cite> <he>למ׳ … עד שימסור למ׳ וכ׳</he> he who dedicates a child to M., is not punishable until he surrenders it to M. and passes it through fire.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 64a:20">Ib. 64ᵃ</cite> <he>קתני עכו״ם וקתני מ׳</he> the Mishnah speaks first of idolatry (in general) and then of M.; <he>מ׳ לאו עכו״ם היא</he> (sub. <he>עבודת</he>) the Molekh worship is not included in general idolatry. Tosef. ib. X, 5 <he>אחד מ׳ ואחד וכ׳</he> whether he passes his son through fire for M. or for any other idol, he is equally punishable; Snh. l. c. Ib. <he>מפני מה … מ׳ כל שהמליכוהו עליהם וכ׳</he> why does the Torah use the expression Molekh (when meaning any idol)? Whatever people make their ruler (<cite ref="M01572"><he>מֶלֶךְ</he></cite>); Y. ib. VII, 25ᶜ top. Bab. ib. l. c. <he>מ׳ עראי</he> an improvised object of worship (a stone, piece of wood &c.); a. fr.
